title: Multimodal language models extract seizure semiology and support patient-held-out seizure classification
summary: An October 2025 preprint analyzed 90 video-EEG-confirmed events from 29 patients at one epilepsy-monitoring unit using vision-language and audio-language models to extract clinical features. With leave-one-patient-out testing, KNN using automated features achieved F1 and AUC of 0.76, below the classifier using expert features. Automated feature extraction itself had mean F1 of 0.51 against expert annotations, and the small retrospective cohort does not establish clinical utility or external generalization. A later journal version was dated November 2026; the detailed results here describe the accessible preprint.
ai_technology: InternVL vision-language models and Qwen audio/vision-language models with downstream KNN and other classifiers
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; University of Alabama at Birmingham

evidence.tested: Ninety video-EEG-confirmed events from 29 patients; open-source vision/audio-language feature extraction and leave-one-patient-out ES/NES classification. Automated-feature KNN F1/AUC were0.76, and feature extraction meanF1 was0.51 versus experts; all results are from the accessible preprint.
evidence.unknown: External multicenter performance, prospective clinical workflow utility and improvement in patient outcomes are unestablished. Detailed final-journal methods/results were not independently read.
evidence.ai_role: Vision-language and audio-language models extract clinical seizure semiology from patient video/audio; classifier evaluation shows moderate patient-held-out discrimination between video-EEG-confirmed epileptic and nonepileptic events.

source_review.scope: Europe PMC XML full text of medRxiv preprint, including methods, patient cohort, MLLM operations, LOPO protocol and results; publisher-deposited final journal abstract and DOI date metadata.
